_comment: Permission rules for the Fabric agent. Reads run freely, anything that writes or consumes capacity asks, destructive operations are denied.
_comment_fences: Identity is the first fence: the agent's identity (see docs/security_and_access.md, Identity) holds Contributor on the development workspaces only. These rules are the second fence and never replace the first.
_comment_change_control: This is a kit file. Change it only through a recorded change (CHG-### in agent_output/change_log.md) so it can be carried forward on upgrade. Per-operator values belong in the git-ignored settings.local.json.
_comment_capacity: Notebook jobs and Livy statements consume capacity, and a Livy statement can run any Spark code, including writes. Both ask every time, even inside a session the operator has already approved.
_comment_deny: mcp__powerbi-modeling-mcp blocks a second registration of the same server under another name, so all modeling calls go through the ask rule for mcp__powerbi-modeling.
_comment_eula: The powerbi-modeling server has an accept_eula tool that accepts Microsoft's EULA and stores the acceptance. Only the lead operator decides on the EULA (SETUP.md step 7), so the agent may never call it.
_comment_fabric_deletes: The fabric MCP server tools that delete an item, a folder or landed data (delete_item, delete_folder, delete_lakehouse_file) are denied, because the agent never deletes an item or landed data (AGENTS.md rule 6). Check the server's tool list whenever its pinned version changes, and deny any new tool that deletes an item or data. The powerbi-modeling server has no separate delete tools, so its deletes cannot be denied by name; every call to it asks.
_comment_fabric_ask: These are listed so that it is explicit that they ask every time. Tools that remove a part of an item (a semantic model table, measure or relationship, or a pipeline activity) change the item rather than delete it, and run only as steps of an approved plan. rename_item runs only as a step of a plan that covers the rename in full (AGENTS.md rule 3). execute_sql_statement can change or remove data. The operator reads the call before approving.
_comment_az_rest: The Azure CLI uses the last --method given, so 'az rest --method get ... --method delete' sends a DELETE. A get call that names a method a second time (--method, an abbreviation such as --meth, or -m) therefore asks, and a delete is denied wherever --method delete or -m delete appears in the command. These rules match the text of the command and are not a security boundary: a command written another way falls back to asking, and the allow rule for get does not limit which host --url names or which token --resource attaches (see Known limitations in KIT_CHANGELOG.md). The agent's identity remains the first fence.
_comment_powershell: Claude Code's PowerShell tool is denied outright, so the agent runs every command through the Bash tool (Git Bash on Windows, installed in SETUP.md step 1). The command rules here are written for Bash and do not restrict the PowerShell tool, and Claude Code does not document that the Read deny rules stop a PowerShell command from reading the key folder or the project Azure CLI profile. Do not replace this with scoped PowerShell(...) rules without adding and testing an equivalent of every Bash rule and of the credential folder rules: a scoped PowerShell rule keeps the tool switched on.
